The SNGL library

Every package of the embedded library. Only sngl:builtin is in scope without an import.

  • sngl:async Handing a closure somewhere else to run.
  • sngl:build Families, and the build-target tree: the two families an `output` directive is written from.
  • sngl:builtin The ambient built-ins: always in scope, and never imported -- importing `sngl:builtin` explicitly is an error.
  • sngl:dialog Host-native modal surfaces: the notifications and file choosers an application asks the platform for rather than draws itself.
  • sngl:i18n Translation and locale-aware formatting.
  • sngl:macro The marks a package writes to say what its declarations mean to the compiler.
  • sngl:math Mathematical constants.
  • sngl:remote Values that arrive from outside the program: what a query, an API call or a database row is to the program *before* it has answered.
  • sngl:remote/http HTTP as a data source: a request whose answer is a `remote.Value`.
  • sngl:seq Integer sequences: the `iter<int>` a counting loop iterates.
  • sngl:test The test facility: the receiver a test function's first parameter carries.
  • sngl:time Dates, clock values and the passage of time: the `date` or `time` a value falls on, the `duration` between two of them, and the `timer` that fires every duration.
  • sngl:tree Segmented component trees: a tree whose nodes are not interchangeable widgets but members of a named family, where a container accepts only its own family's members.
  • sngl:ui The user interface: the components most applications are built from, and the vocabulary they share.
  • sngl:ui/draw 2D shapes and the canvas that hosts them, and the `shape` tree they are members of.
  • sngl:ui/markup Inline rich text: the `span` family, and the `richText` node that shows a run of it.
  • sngl:ui/markup/md Markdown's vocabulary: what the `md:` import scheme reads, and `document`, which parses markdown written as a string while the program builds.
  • sngl:ui/nav Navigation: the pages of an application and the navigators that hold them.
  • sngl:x/c Package c is what a SNGL package says about the C library its `#[cnative]` declarations name: the header a cgo preamble includes, and the flags it compiles and links with.
  • sngl:x/gen Package gen is what a target package says about what it generates.
  • sngl:x/gen/cache Package cache is what a generated file says it was generated from.
  • sngl:x/gen/trust Package trust is the vocabulary of the user's grants: what code a project brought may do on the machine that builds it.
  • sngl:x/scheme/c Package c serves the `c:` import scheme: the library's own plugin, which a program reaches by importing `c:…` and never by importing this package.
  • sngl:x/scheme/gir The `gir:` import scheme: a GObject library's widgets, declared from its introspection data.
